scope: Native-keyed loaded-resource provider cache, World acquisition and simulation-owned readmission; ready-resource profile and cold-result publication primitives

cases.expected: ASCII case-only authored model variants share a canonical loaded resource. Slash variants keep distinct identities even when normalized VFS path and file hash agree. Embedded NUL follows C-string semantics.

Cache entries are nonowning and disappear at the last canonical handle release. Retained renderer aliases and uncached source artifacts keep KF data without pinning the loaded-info identity. Reacquisition after backend eviction can obtain replacement bytes.

find performs no load; independent loaded candidates reconcile at publishLoaded. First resident native key wins even when another candidate has different parsed bytes/fingerprint. No worker scheduling or fixed pending delay is invented.
cases.original: 4378F0 / 435B10; pending-cache05 actual pending map/cache publication courses

cases.expected: admit checks the supplied validated source path and fingerprint and rejects a conflicting resident. This is separate from native job publication. It does not itself audit physical filesystem freshness.
Resource bytes remain usable after the provider facade is destroyed; cleanup does not dereference a retired provider.
Missing, malformed, non-KF and multiplexed resources cannot populate the pool.
Concurrent ready acquisitions share one live canonical identity; an expired predecessor cannot erase a newer entry under the same key; all entries reclaim after ownership ends.
Two actors in one World share the native provider pool. Backend eviction and a changed file do not replace still-resident info or publish either renderer source list.

A valid incoming current resource can be validated in a fresh cache despite a different live resident. Validation preserves the live snapshot and its next cache hit. Changed-byte cases explicitly evict the backend cache before the resource-service audit.
Retain/detach, candidate clear and rollback restore the original provider context with its original resident bytes.

Readmission accepts a cached NI source after every request is gone without fabricating request slots. Source artifacts and request-backed canonical info leases occupy separate maps; portable resource/request/NI identities are unchanged.
cases.coverage_limit: Headless admission and source/slot inspection; no live renderer reconstruction or request destructor caller.

cases.expected: Repeated ready-resource preparation uses resident info across backend eviction. Saved source audit still rejects a fingerprint that differs from the resource service.
cases.correction: Previous assertion expected a new file hash on a resident native-key hit. Actual 4383B0 hit/release evidence establishes resident reuse until final ownership ends.

cases.expected: 402E30 with the actual 474C50 format/directory literals unconditionally prefixes Meshes\ and preserves slash/dot spelling until C-string termination. Already-prefixed input receives a second prefix.
cases.boundary: Actual formatter and CRT, heap/OS shims; no filesystem loading or native game process.

not_accepted: Live GetUp request/NI graph factory or dispatcher
Worker scheduling and pending-IO fresh-process restoration
Native NI-manager registration order integration and renderer restoration
Original filesystem-loading equivalence for all prefix/dot spellings; generic ResourceSystem backend path mapping is unchanged
Physical filesystem hot-reload freshness without backend invalidation
Normal-input view/device/FPS, recovery and canonical fresh-save courses
